WIC26A-01.explanation: Baskets made to carry fish ended up among city furnishings while the crews switched to crates, so the purchases "repurposed" the craft, turning it to a new use. "Rekindled" fails because households wove about as many baskets as they always had; the craft never lapsed. "Professionalized" fails because the same households did the weaving. "Petrified" fails because the passage reports a change in what the baskets were for, not a freezing of their form.

WIC26A-02.explanation: Every district's cutting limit came from a table built on the valley's count and updated only when the valley was recounted, so the valley stood for all fourteen as the service's "proxy." "Prototype" fails because nothing was built in the valley and then copied; only its figures were used. "Outpost" fails because the passage describes a survey, not a remote station. "Reservoir" fails because the service took figures from the valley, not a supply it held back and drew on.

WIC26A-03.explanation: The weavers' hall lost its walls while blocks carved with a weaver's shuttle turned up in houses and a bridge across town, so it served as the town's "quarry," a source of building stone. "Refuge" fails because a roofless ruin sheltered no one. "Platform" fails because no one spoke from the hall. "Ornament" fails because the hall was left to fall apart, and its carving survived only in foundations.

WIC26A-04.explanation: Brick drains took over the ditches' work, houses now stand where the channels ran, and no muster has been held since 1858, so the rule, though never repealed, had become "obsolete." "Onerous" fails because no one was being made to do the work at all. "Profitable" fails because with no muster there was no fine to collect. "Porous" fails because the rule was not riddled with exemptions; it simply had nothing left to apply to.

WIC26A-05.explanation: The gardener plants, uproots and replants the same roses, and the narrator, who explains everyone else, never explains him, so he is the novel's "puzzle." "Prism" fails because the story is not told from his point of view. "Pivot" fails because his acts go unnoticed and change nothing in the plot. "Pawn" fails because no one directs him; he acts on his own, for reasons no one gives.

WIC26A-06.explanation: The survey's discovery of shallow molten rock drew all later work toward itself, leaving the ridge idea a single line in the textbooks and its planned test undone, so the survey "overshadowed" the hypothesis. "Rehabilitated" fails because the hypothesis was never discredited and gained no new support. "Pruned" fails because nothing was cut from it; it went untested. "Orphaned" fails because nothing the hypothesis rested on was overturned; it was still stated, just eclipsed.

WIC26A-07.explanation: Where rivals copied old errors, the surveyor spent eleven summers measuring roads and plotting towns himself, and a later survey found his distances nearly exact, so the map was "rigorous." "Prescient" fails because the map recorded what existed accurately rather than anticipating what would come. "Provincial" fails because his measurements covered the whole kingdom. "Portable" fails because nothing is said about the map's size or how it was carried.

WIC26A-08.explanation: Families read the column aloud every weekend in a fixed way, even though it said almost the same thing each week, so it was the city's "ritual," valued for the practice rather than the content. "Portal" fails because the column brought in no news of the outside world. "Rudder" fails because it offered nothing that steered the city's decisions. "Rampart" fails because nothing threatened the city that the column defended against.

WIC26B-01.explanation: The owners took over every other institution, the weavers' repealed rules lived on only inside the hall, and the hall withstood yearly attempts to buy it; combining these shows it was the place the weavers held against the owners, their "stronghold." "Springboard" fails because the weavers were keeping their trade's rules, not using the hall to leave the trade. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's value lay in being held against the owners, not in being displayed. "Switchboard" fails because nothing in the passage passes through the hall from one party to another.

WIC26B-02.explanation: The truce was signed and toasted every year, while weir-cutting never fell below its old rate in any year and no one was punished; combining these shows the truce existed in name only, so it was "token." "Tacit" fails because the truce was signed openly. "Tactical" fails because a truce made for an aim still holds while the aim lasts, and this one never held in any year. "Unilateral" fails because neither town held back.

WIC26B-03.explanation: The pages were ruined when found, the editor worked on them for three years, and the printed book turned out to contain nearly every scene the novelist described, so the editor "salvaged" the book. "Sanitized" fails because nearly every scene survives; nothing was cut for propriety. "Shelved" fails because the three years went into work on the pages, after which the book was printed. "Updated" fails because the only differences from the novelist's plan are lines lost to the water.

WIC26B-04.explanation: Only the excess water above a set level leaves the river, runs across the hard clay and out to the bay by the creeks within a night, and the lower river is spared the flood; combining these shows the marsh carries off surplus water, so it is "a kind of spillway." "Sponge" fails because the clay floor takes nothing in and the creeks are back to normal by morning. "Sieve" fails because the marsh changes how much water reaches the lower river, not what is in it. "Seedbed" fails because nothing in the passage begins life in the marsh.

WIC26B-05.explanation: The rule rewarded sheer weight in the forwards, so the colliery clubs, with the heaviest men, began winning almost every match and every title: the rule "unbalanced" the game. "Tamed" fails because the rule did nothing to make play less rough; it made strength decisive. "Splintered" fails because the clubs stayed in one league competing for one title. "Urbanized" fails because the clubs that rose were village clubs that already belonged to the league.

WIC26B-06.explanation: The secretary learned the chairman's work, filled in whenever the chairman was ill, and finally succeeded to the chair, so the secretary was the council's "understudy." "Scapegoat" fails because nothing in the passage shows the secretary being blamed. "Watchdog" fails because the secretary worked alongside the chairman rather than checking the members. "Tiebreaker" fails because the secretary's role was to take the chairman's place, not to decide divided votes.

WIC26B-07.explanation: The record took a funeral hymn, removed its prayer, and sent it to the dance halls, so the recording "secularized" the ballad. "Standardized" fails because the passage concerns where and why the ballad was sung, not the number of versions. "Sweetened" fails because the record kept the hill singers' hard sound. "Unearthed" fails because the ballad was already sung at every funeral in the hill counties.

WIC26B-08.explanation: Ships could only use the strait with a paper bought at the island's harbor office, and those receipts funded a navy, so the empire valued the island as its "tollgate." "Storehouse" fails because ships sailed on with their cargo after getting the paper. "Watchtower" fails because the island's role was charging ships for passage, not watching for enemies. "Trophy" fails because the island produced large revenues.

WIC26C-01.explanation: Each time the eastern lord built up force, the monastery built up an answering force of its own, tenants and church backing, and the march never came, so the monastery held the balance: it was the region's "counterweight." "Checkpoint" fails because the lord is deterred by what the monastery could raise, not stopped at a gate; "broker" fails because the monastery answers one side's threat instead of arranging terms; "custodian" fails because it holds its own land and keeps nothing in trust for anyone.

WIC26C-02.explanation: The new hospital could not be equipped from the budget, its wards opened with machines and surgeons transferred from the county, and the county hospital ended as a part-time clinic, so the board "cannibalized" the county hospital. "Certified" fails because no standard the hospital met is described, only its emptying; "cloned" fails because the city hospital received the county hospital's own machines and surgeons rather than being built as a copy; "bartered" fails because the board moved its own property between its own hospitals and traded with no one.

WIC26C-03.explanation: The ministry moved fast and openly, but with no measurement at all: one sum handed to anyone at the door whatever the loss, and sandbags dumped unfilled, so the response was "crude." "Covert" fails because the ministry's trucks delivered the aid in the open; "complacent" fails because it acted within a day; "bureaucratic" fails because there were no claims, no records, not even names: the opposite of procedure.

WIC26C-04.explanation: She moved from washing glass to doing his syntheses step by step under his eye, then inherited his laboratory and kept his methods exactly, so she was the chemist's "apprentice." "Audience" fails because she learned by doing the work, not by listening; "ambassador" fails because everything she does is inside the laboratory, and she represents him to no one; "accomplice" fails because what she carries on is his method, openly, not any wrongdoing.

WIC26C-05.explanation: The house bought nearly all the grain and all the storage, and afterward the price rose with steady harvests to whatever its agent posted, so it controlled supply and price: it "cornered" the town's grain trade. "Awakened" fails because farmers had long sold grain in the town; "bankrolled" fails because the house bought the grain itself rather than funding others; "coordinated" fails because, holding the harvest and both warehouses, it took the trade over rather than organizing other dealers.

WIC26C-06.explanation: A room three stories tall, roofed in glass so that daylight alone lit it, is spacious and full of light: the building was "airy." "Austere" fails because the room has tiled murals and potted trees, not bare surfaces; "adaptable" fails because nothing about the room can be moved or changed; "accessible" fails because the main room sits on the top floor and nothing is said of ease of entry.

WIC26C-07.explanation: Her private doubts appear only in letters to him, and he alone knew of her decision and kept it until her death, so he was the poet's "confidant." "Critic" fails because what reached him was her private life, not poems to judge; "courier" fails because what she told him went no further; "benefactor" fails because nothing passes from him to her but his silence, with no money or support described.

WIC26C-08.explanation: The phrase the children knew is the tune's first eight bars of thirty-two, and the symphony repeats that phrase alone to the end, so the composer "clipped" the tune: he cut it short. "Braided" fails because nothing else is joined to it; the movement just repeats the phrase; "animated" fails because it keeps the fiddlers' own speed; "cleansed" fails because the phrase keeps every note.

WIC26D-01.explanation: The trustees decided what to ask, she then spent weeks where the state and county officials sat, and the replies the board debated came back through her, so she was its "envoy," the representative it sent to outside parties. "Gatekeeper" fails because she did not decide what the board considered; the trustees settled the requests and debated the replies. "Figurehead" fails because weeks of dealing with officials was real work, not a title. "Holdout" fails because she carried requests the trustees had agreed on together.

WIC26D-02.explanation: A national law listed the procession as a monument, the state funded its upkeep, and an inspector held it each year to its 1951 form, so the changes had "enshrined" the custom, preserving it as something honored and protected. "Democratized" fails because the singers had to match the 1951 description, so participation was not opened up. "Dramatized" fails because the event was held to its old form, not restaged as a show. "Harmonized" fails because each village's procession was kept as described rather than made uniform.

WIC26D-03.explanation: Inspectors checked carts only where unrelated work happened to take them, so fines piled up on a few blocks while identical carts elsewhere went unvisited: the enforcement was "haphazard," following no plan of its own. "Evenhanded" fails because vendors doing the same thing were treated very differently depending on location. "Furtive" fails because nothing suggests the inspectors concealed their checks. "Drastic" fails because the passage describes how unevenly enforcement fell, not how severe its penalties were.

WIC26D-04.explanation: The fungus rotted only the anchoring roots, so the full-grown trees leaned further each year until they lay on the ground, roots rotted through: the outbreak had "felled" the oaks. "Dwarfed" fails because the trees were full-size, with sound trunks and full crowns, when they came down. "Defoliated" fails because the fungus attacked roots and left the crowns in leaf. "Honeycombed" fails because the trunks stayed sound; the damage was below ground.

WIC26D-05.explanation: Its arguments were familiar and its pages largely unopened, while huge penny runs paid for halls and lawyers, so the pamphlet was the movement's "fundraiser." "Handbook" fails because its pages held arguments, not procedures, and most copies were never opened past the start. "Gospel" fails because a pamphlet repeating commonplace arguments, left unread, was not the movement's revered authority. "Foil" fails because the movement printed and sold it itself rather than arguing against it.

WIC26D-06.explanation: A fast, shallow wall of water left trees and stalks rooted in undisturbed soil yet showed from above as stripes running with the current, so it had laid them over: the flood had "flattened" the valley's growth. "Dammed" fails because the water was gone within hours. "Gouged" fails because the soil was barely disturbed. "Emptied" fails because the trees and crops stayed rooted where they grew.

WIC26D-07.explanation: Disasters get the same tone as seed prices, and the funniest details are passed over as quickly as anything else, so the humor comes from an unchanged, expressionless delivery: the prose is "deadpan." "Didactic" fails because he moves on from each event without drawing anything from it. "Digressive" fails because the chapter moves from one event of the winter to the next. "Florid" fails because he describes catastrophe in the voice he uses for seed prices, the reverse of ornate.

WIC26D-08.explanation: The army placed regiments at the town so they could reach the port's docks within an hour, and they trained there and went to the city only when called, so the town had become the city's "garrison," the base of the force that defended it. "Dormitory" fails because the soldiers spent their days in the town and went to the city only on alert, rather than working there daily. "Getaway" fails because those arriving were stationed troops, not city people seeking leisure. "Granary" fails because the town lived on the soldiers' pay, not on grain.

WIC26E-01.explanation: Every buyer paid a little extra into a sum the yard kept apart, and that sum rebuilt the boats of whoever suffered a loss, so the yard served as the coast's "insurer." "Lender" fails because the new hulls were handed over at no charge and were never repaid; "memory" fails because the passage describes money held against losses, not a record of the coast's past; "incubator" fails because the yard restored existing fishing families rather than raising up new enterprises that went off on their own.

WIC26E-02.explanation: The miners' letters told the valley nothing new; the paper's role was to carry those complaints, unchanged, to audiences far beyond it, so it served as the miners' "megaphone." "Lens" fails because the miners already knew about the cheating, so the paper did not change how they saw anything; "jury" fails because the paper printed the letters as written and passed no judgment; "ladder" fails because nothing helped miners rise to better positions.

WIC26E-03.explanation: The report replaced one shared estimate with conflicting figures, each side picked its own, and the legislature could not proceed without yet another estimate, so the report "muddied" the debate. "Launched" fails because removal had been argued for a decade; "legitimized" fails because both sides were already arguing in the open from an official estimate; "jolted" fails because the report led to a postponed vote, not to sudden movement.

WIC26E-04.explanation: After thousands of productions, her reviews dwindled and she dismissed as familiar plays that others found fresh, so she had become "jaded." "Judicious" fails because the plays she waved off succeeded, so her verdicts did not reflect sound judgment; "mercurial" fails because her response was the same dismissal again and again; "insistent" fails because she was pressing no demand, only losing interest.

WIC26E-05.explanation: She solved the problem of seeing into a dark box without disturbing it by borrowing a dentist's mirror and pairing it with a knitting needle and a flashlight, so her approach was "ingenious." "Intrusive" fails because the device existed so the lid would never be lifted; "methodical" fails because the passage describes one clever solution, not a fixed routine; "literary" fails because nothing concerns how she wrote up what she saw.

WIC26E-06.explanation: Every other clause was written in terms the seventh defined, so when it was struck down the states had to rebuild the whole treaty: it was the treaty's "keystone." "Loophole" fails because the clause let no party escape its obligations, and the court removed it for an outdated gauge, not for abuse; "lever" fails because no state used it to pressure the other; "lottery" fails because it was a fixed method of measurement, not a matter of chance.

WIC26E-07.explanation: Slow unloading, tiny discrepancies recorded, and reports later found exact to the last item together show he was "meticulous." "Naive" fails because he checked the crates against the ships' papers rather than accepting them; "lenient" fails because the passage reports how closely he checked, not how mildly he punished; "incorruptible" fails because nothing concerns bribes or attempts to sway him.

WIC26E-08.explanation: The singers joined the ballad to a second printed song so smoothly that no one could find the seam, so singing had "merged" the ballad with another. "Mangled" fails because the joined song is seamless and makes sense, with the sailor's name fitted into the lament; "mellowed" fails because the sailor's fate is not softened: grief is added to it; "moralized" fails because the added verses mourn rather than teach a lesson.
